name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rob Menendez running with large fundraising edge
No Republican on the ballot; independent challengers underfunded
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The seat sits in a heavily Democratic district and Menendez has raised nearly $2 million with outside support, while the opposition consists of independents with no visible fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win around 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or a well-funded independent surge could narrow the margin, though a Democratic loss remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Rob Menendez, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that leans about 15 points Democratic. He has raised nearly $2 million and holds a large financial advantage, with outside groups adding support and no recorded opposition spending. No Republican appears on the ballot; the challengers are independents with no reported fundraising.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 95%. The race is rated Safe D, with the incumbent heavily favored to hold the seat.
